sentences.text: Permit controls coordinate approved work scope, electrical isolation, field execution, and return to service without treating authorization as proof of a safe electrical state.
The Duty Planner submits a defined task scope, work location, crew, and requested operating window for review.
The Field Supervisor confirms that the proposed method, access arrangements, and work party are suitable for the task.
Redoubt shall block permit release until required risk reviews and isolation references are complete.
The HSE Officer reviews task hazards and confirms that required controls are assigned before the permit is authorized.
The Weather Analyst uses the Wave Burst Record to assess whether the planned access period remains suitable.
The Port Agent issues the Berth Slot Confirmation for the planned work period.
The Electrical Technician identifies the electrical sources, isolation points, and verification steps required by the approved scope.
The Substation Operator applies authorized switching actions and records the resulting equipment state.
For turbine work, the Electrical Technician verifies the relevant local isolation and secures the equipment against unintended energization.
Turbine Lockout is maintained while personnel are exposed to the identified hazards.
Work begins only after the Field Supervisor confirms that the permit is active and the required isolations have been independently verified.
The Field Supervisor briefs the crew on the permit limits, isolation boundaries, communications, and conditions requiring work to stop.
The Electrical Technician proves the test instrument, tests for absence of voltage, and proves the instrument again where the procedure requires it.
The Personnel Tracking Console supports confirmation that personnel assigned to the task are accounted for at the work location.
A change in equipment condition, task scope, or operating constraint requires the Field Supervisor to pause work and reassess the authorization.
The Duty Planner coordinates any revised work window with the relevant operational roles before the permit is amended.
The Field Supervisor confirms that tools, temporary connections, and personnel are clear before requesting isolation removal.
The Electrical Technician checks that the work area is ready for restoration and reports any outstanding defects or restrictions.
The Substation Operator removes isolations only under the approved switching process and records each restoration action.
The Control Engineer reviews the restored equipment state and confirms that required operational checks are complete.
The Shore Control Room retains the permit status, isolation history, test results, and restoration decision for operational review.
The Duty Planner closes the work authorization after the Field Supervisor confirms completion or formally records any remaining work.
Equipment returns to service only when operating personnel accept the restored condition and any applicable restrictions are communicated.
